answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before earning influence, then randomly assign verified tasks and slash deposits when identities submit mutually inconsistent work or fail agreed checks. Splitting one attacker’s funds across a hundred names does not create more economic weight: each name needs its own capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. A juniper-tagged task in the lagoon may be sampled again as the tide changes, making cheap, disposable identities costly to sustain.
